title: Files, Content, Notes, Libraries, and document-management boundaries
objectives: Map an uploaded file to ContentDocument (identity), ContentVersion (this binary), ContentDocumentLink (who/where it is shared), and ContentDistribution (external public link).
Place Notes (ContentNote) and Libraries (Content Workspace) on that same Files model, not as Attachment or Document (Classic) first choices.
Choose record-linked Files versus a Library versus a public ContentDistribution versus Knowledge (APP-004).
State API rules: create files via ContentVersion; query share locations via ContentDocumentLink.
diagnostic_question: A PDF must live on an Opportunity, be versioned, be visible to a teammate, sit in a team library, and later get a time-boxed public URL. Which objects do you create, and which Classic Attachment or Knowledge article would you refuse?
definition: Salesforce Files is not one table. ContentDocument is the document identity uploaded to Salesforce Files or Salesforce CRM Content. ContentVersion is a specific binary version of that document. ContentDocumentLink is the share row to a user, group, record, or library (and to ContentNote). ContentDistribution is information about sharing a document externally via a public URL. Notes and Libraries use this model; Classic Attachment/Document are legacy boundaries. ([ContentDocument](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentdocument.htm); [ContentVersion](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentversion.htm); [ContentDocumentLink](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentdocumentlink.htm); [Standard Objects list — ContentDistribution](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_list.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail people who SOQL ContentDocument to 'upload a file,' who treat Attachment as the Lightning Files model, who confuse a Library with Knowledge, or who email a perpetual public link when they needed a ContentDocumentLink to a private record. Sharing is the link row, not the binary.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a film production. ContentDocument is the movie's identity—the title that stays as cuts change. ContentVersion is this cut of the film, the actual frames. ContentDocumentLink is a screening pass: who (user, group, record, library) may see that title. ContentDistribution is a public trailer URL that can expire. Notes are sticky-script pages in the same vault. Libraries are studio rooms that hold titles. You do not create the movie by inserting the identity first; you publish a cut (ContentVersion) and the identity appears.
deeper_explanation: ContentDocument represents a document uploaded to a library in Salesforce Files or Salesforce CRM Content (API 21.0+ for Files; 17.0+ for CRM Content). LatestPublishedVersionId points at the current ContentVersion. Use ContentDocument to retrieve, query, update, and delete the latest version; use ContentVersion to create and version. To create a document, insert ContentVersion without ContentDocumentId—the parent ContentDocument is created automatically. To add a revision, set an existing ContentDocumentId. ([ContentDocument](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentdocument.htm))

ContentVersion is a specific version of a document in CRM Content or Files. FirstPublishLocationId can be a user (personal files), a library, or other ContentDocumentLink-supported records so you create and share in one transaction. ([ContentVersion](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentversion.htm))

ContentDocumentLink is the link between a CRM Content document, Salesforce file, or ContentNote and where it is shared: users, groups, records (including custom objects that support feed tracking), and CRM Content libraries. Query it to see locations or files at a location. A ContentDocument delete cascades links; that cascade does not fire ContentDocumentLink delete triggers. ([ContentDocumentLink](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_contentdocumentlink.htm))

ContentDistribution represents information about sharing a document externally (API 32.0+). It is the public/expiring-link object, not the share-to-a-record object. ([Standard Objects](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.object_reference.meta/object_reference/sforce_api_objects_list.htm))

Notes in Lightning are ContentNote files in this model, linked with ContentDocumentLink. Libraries are Content Workspace rooms with membership—still Files, not Knowledge articles (APP-004) and not Chatter posts (APP-005). Classic Attachment and Document remain conversion/legacy boundaries; do not design new Lightning apps on Attachment. File size and org storage caps: Needs verification in current Help.

mental_model.analogy: Film production: ContentDocument = the movie identity/title, ContentVersion = this cut of the film, ContentDocumentLink = screening pass (user/group/record/library), ContentDistribution = public trailer URL, Note = sticky script page, Library = studio room.
useful_mapping: Uploaded bytes → stored on a ContentVersion
Stable file Id users talk about → ContentDocument
Share to Opportunity → ContentDocumentLink to the record
Share to a team room → ContentDocumentLink to a Library (Content Workspace)
Public URL for a customer → ContentDistribution
Insert path → ContentVersion first, ContentDocument created for you
Knowledge article → different product (APP-004), not a Library
where_it_breaks: Changing ContentDocument owner deletes/inserts ContentDocumentLink rows to owners.
Cascaded link deletes on file delete do not run ContentDocumentLink triggers.
A public distribution is not a Salesforce user share.
The analogy does not encode storage quotas, virus scan, or Files Connect to external drives.

claims.claim: ContentDocument represents a document uploaded to Salesforce Files or Salesforce CRM Content. To create a document, create a ContentVersion without ContentDocumentId; the parent ContentDocument is created automatically. New versions require an existing ContentDocumentId.

ContentVersion represents a specific version of a document. FirstPublishLocationId can be a user, a public library, or other records supported by ContentDocumentLink so the first share happens in the same transaction.

ContentDocumentLink represents the link between a CRM Content document, Salesforce file, or ContentNote and where it is shared (users, groups, records, libraries). Use it to query share locations. Cascaded link deletes from ContentDocument delete do not fire ContentDocumentLink triggers.
ContentDistribution represents information about sharing a document externally (API 32.0+).
claims.validation: Standard Objects catalog definition of ContentDistribution.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Files split identity, binary, share, and public URL. ContentDocument is identity. ContentVersion is this binary—insert it to create the file. ContentDocumentLink is who can see it (user, group, record, library, note). ContentDistribution is an external link. Do not start new apps on Classic Attachment.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I draw File to ContentDocument to ContentVersion, then branch to ContentDocumentLink and ContentDistribution. I query links to debug 'I cannot see the file.' I use FirstPublishLocationId when I want the first share in one transaction. Libraries are rooms, Knowledge is articles, Chatter is the wall. Notes are ContentNote in the same graph. Owner changes rebuild owner links. Cascaded deletes skip link triggers—I will not put logic only on those triggers.

interview_questions.question: Draw the Files objects and their jobs.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: ContentDocument is identity. ContentVersion is this binary. ContentDocumentLink is who can see it. ContentDistribution is an external URL. Create by inserting ContentVersion, not ContentDocument.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I mention Files versus CRM Content API versions only at a high level. FirstPublishLocationId can attach the first share. Notes are ContentNote. Libraries are link targets. I query links to debug visibility. I will not design on Attachment. Cascade delete skips link triggers.
interview_questions.example: LAB_SOW.pdf: one document, two versions, links to Opportunity and LAB_Legal, optional distribution.
tradeoffs: Record link vs library vs public URL

interview_questions.question: How do you upload a file in Apex?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Insert ContentVersion with VersionData and PathOnClient, no ContentDocumentId. Set FirstPublishLocationId if you want the first share in the same transaction.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: For version 2 I pass ContentDocumentId. I add extra ContentDocumentLink rows for more records or a library. I do not insert ContentDocument. I consider trigger recursion on ContentDocument insert when a file is added to a library, as the object page notes.

interview_questions.question: Legal wants SOWs in a team room and on each Opportunity, plus a customer preview link.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: One file: Version on the Opportunity, extra ContentDocumentLink to the Library, ContentDistribution for the customer. Do not upload three copies.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I warn that a public URL is a different trust boundary than a Salesforce user link. I prefer expiry. I keep Knowledge out. Notes can capture negotiation recap as ContentNote. I verify library membership separately from Opportunity sharing.
interview_questions.example: LAB_SOW one ContentDocument, two links, one distribution.
tradeoffs: Public URL vs Experience Cloud login

interview_questions.question: A team stores SOPs as PDFs in a Library and calls it Knowledge.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I redirect them. Libraries are Files rooms. Knowledge is published articles with channels and categories (APP-004). PDFs can attach to articles, but the corpus is Knowledge.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Search, translation, data categories, and portal channels are why Knowledge exists. A Library is the right place for working SOWs, not for the service SOP corpus. I will not fight storing a PDF, but I will not let it replace article publication.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Reset_VPN as a Knowledge article; LAB_SOW.pdf in LAB_Legal library.

interview_questions.question: User can upload to an Opportunity but a teammate cannot see the file.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Query ContentDocumentLink. They need a link—or access to the linked record or library. Upload success is not visibility.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish file share from Opportunity OWD. A private file on a shared Opportunity can still hide. I check whether FirstPublishLocationId was only the uploader's personal files. I add a link to the record or library. I do not re-upload.
interview_questions.example: Link ShareType/Visibility leaves it owner-only; teammate has Opportunity Read but no file link.
tradeoffs: Record-level file visibility vs explicit user links
follow_ups: What does ShareType V/I/C mean? (open field help)

interview_questions.question: A trigger on ContentDocumentLink delete never fires when users delete Files from the UI.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If they deleted the ContentDocument, cascaded link deletes do not fire ContentDocumentLink triggers. Put the logic on ContentDocument delete.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce: delete the file versus remove one share. Removing one link should fire the link trigger; deleting the document may not. I cite the Object Reference. I do not 'fix' it by converting to Attachment.
interview_questions.example: Delete LAB_SOW from Files related list; document delete cascade skips link trigger.
weak_answer_warnings: Assuming the trigger is not deployed

interview_questions.question: When do you refuse ContentDistribution?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the audience has Salesforce access (use a link), when the file is confidential without expiry/password controls, or when a portal login is the real requirement.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: External sharing information is powerful and easy to forward. I prefer Experience Cloud or a record the customer can log into. If we must distribute, I set expiry and review who can create distributions. I still version via ContentVersion internally.
interview_questions.example: Internal SOW: Opportunity plus LAB_Legal links only. No distribution.
weak_answer_warnings: Public links as the default share

interview_questions.question: Teach Files with the film-production analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Title is ContentDocument, this cut is ContentVersion, screening pass is ContentDocumentLink, public trailer is ContentDistribution, sticky script is Note, studio room is Library.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: It breaks on owner-change link rewrite, cascade trigger skip, and the fact that Knowledge is not a studio room. I then quote the create path: Version without Document Id. I mention FirstPublishLocationId. I refuse Attachment for new Lightning work. I keep Chatter and Knowledge in their own topics.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard mermaid: File → ContentDocument → ContentVersion → Link and Distribution.
follow_ups: Where do AppExchange apps store files? (APP-007)
Where do Case emails attach? (still Files or email attachments—verify)
